issuing_body: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota
title: Five Defendants Found Guilty for Their Roles in $250 Million Fraud Scheme
supports: Following a six-week trial before Judge Nancy E. Brasel, the federal jury convicted Abdiaziz Shafii Farah, Mohamed Jama Ismail, Abdimajid Mohamed Nur, Mukhtar Mohamed Shariff, and Hayat Mohamed Nur.

Abdiaziz Shafii Farah was convicted of one count conspiracy to commit wire fraud, six wire-fraud counts, one count conspiracy to commit federal-programs bribery, two federal-programs-bribery counts, one count conspiracy to commit money laundering, eleven money-laundering counts, and one count false statements in a passport application.
Mohamed Jama Ismail was convicted of one count conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one count conspiracy to commit money laundering, and one count money laundering.
Abdimajid Mohamed Nur was convicted of one count conspiracy to commit wire fraud, four wire-fraud counts, one count conspiracy to commit money laundering, and four money-laundering counts.
Mukhtar Mohamed Shariff was convicted of one count conspiracy to commit wire fraud, one wire-fraud count, one count conspiracy to commit money laundering, and one count money laundering.
Hayat Mohamed Nur was convicted of one count conspiracy to commit wire fraud and two wire-fraud counts.
The release states that, as proven at trial, the convicted defendants carried out a $40 million fraud scheme against the Federal Child Nutrition Program.
The release states that at that point seventy defendants had been charged across fourteen indictments and six criminal informations, and eighteen defendants had entered guilty pleas.
does_not_support: The names of the two defendants fully acquitted at the June 7, 2024 trial; this release lists only the five convicted defendants.

A court-certified network-wide proven loss for all Feeding Our Future defendants; the $40 million figure is specific to the trial group described in this release, while the broader $250 million figure is the scheme-wide prosecution characterization.
